newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Controls sees record 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Controls sees record 1997 earnings.

text.p: Johnson Controls Inc said it is confident that 1997 will be its seventh consecutive year of record earnings and 51st year of consecutive sales increases.

The company on Tuesday reported third-quarter sales of $2.88 billion, up from $2.48 billion for the same quarter of fiscal 1996. Income from continuing operations rose to $74.4 million, or $0.81 per share, up from $63.5 million, or $0.69 per share, for the same quarter of fiscal 1996.
Shares in the automotive systems and building controls manufacturer were off 3/8 at 42-1/2.
Third-quarter sales by the company's automotive systems group rose to $2.1 billion from $1.74 billion a year ago.
"The October 1996 acquisition of Prince, an interior systems company based in Michigan, accounted for nearly two-thirds of the revenue increase," the company said.

Automotive systems operating income was up from the 1996 level "despite the impact of the strike at Chrysler Corp's Mound Street facility, which reduced the company's sales of seats, overhead and door systems and other components used in Jeep and other Chrysler vehicles," the company said. "Lost production reduced ... fully diluted earnings in the current quarter by $0.05 per share," Johnson said.
The company said it now holds the largest share of the battery market in North America as a result of growth by its existing customers and the addition of new accounts.
Launch of shipments to fulfill a contract to supply the DieHard Gold battery to Sears Roebuck and Co, which is effective October 1, will further strengthen this market leadership, the company said.
Sales by the controls group rose to $773.6 million for the third quarter, up from 1996's $744.1 million.
